discovery: Quantum cryptography: invention of quantum key distribution (BB84 and entanglement-based E91)

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

nominees.name: Artur K. Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84, 1984) showed that the quantum no-cloning principle and measurement disturbance can guarantee secure communication, founding quantum cryptography. Ekert (1991) independently showed that entanglement and Bell-inequality violation can certify key security, linking foundational tests of nonlocality directly to a technology. Together these ideas turned quantum mechanics from a subject of interpretation into a resource for information processing. They opened the field of quantum information, inspired quantum teleportation (Bennett, Brassard et al., 1993), and set the direction for decades of experiments. These range from fibre networks spanning thousands of kilometres to satellite-to-ground key distribution and entanglement-based, device-independent protocols. Today quantum key distribution is deployed in metropolitan and intercontinental networks, which shows that physical law itself can underpin information security. This is a conceptual discovery of the deepest kind, and it has been fully verified by experiment.
